headline: 🔴 ShinyHunters' Rey detained in Jordan and cooperating with the FBI, 🇰🇷 South Korea's president orders emergency probe into bank data leaks, 🍎 Fake Zoom installer drops CloudSyncD macOS backdoor, 🇩🇰 DTU breach exposes up to 200,000 people via stolen IAM credentials, 🔁 Sygnia publishes NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 exploitation IOCs, 🔐 Bouncy Castle ships critical BC-JAVA crypto fixes
summary: The weekend cycle belongs to ShinyHunters, with alleged member Rey detained in Jordan and reportedly cooperating with the FBI, while South Korea's president ordered an emergency probe into bank data leaks, macOS users faced a fake Zoom backdoor, and Sygnia published new NetScaler exploitation IOCs.

overrides.why: Promoted to lead: the only top-slate story with a fresh, never-covered development (Reuters-reported Jordan detention and FBI cooperation), outranking re-report-only candidates.
Every event since the Oct 2 coverage is outlet roundups re-reporting the known KEV listing and upcoming fixed builds; no new development to state, kept in watchlist.
Today's events re-report Horizon3's single-encoded-character analysis already covered Oct 2; nothing new beyond continued scanning watch.
Weekend events re-report Symantec's attribution and the six additional SharePoint CVEs already carried Oct 2-3; no new victims or confirmed exploitation of the newer flaws.
New events are re-reports of the emergency patch covered yesterday; the 'actively exploited' headline is aggregator-grade with no primary confirmation, kept as watchlist item.
